cards.text: Paul is writing to the believers in Ephesus, and here he reminds them where they started. Not sick, not sleepy, friend: dead in their trespasses and sins. Back then they walked in those sins, going along with the ways of this world and of the ruler of the power of the air.

cards.question: Paul says the ruler of the power of the air is a spirit who is still at work now, in the sons of disobedience.

cards.text: Then Paul describes a whole way of life: fulfilling the cravings of the flesh and indulging its desires and thoughts. That's a craving holding the car keys, baker.

cards.question: Who does Paul say lived that way at one time, fulfilling the cravings of the flesh?

cards.text: Then comes the hardest line yet: "Like the rest, we were by nature children of wrath." That's not one burnt edge, friend, that's the whole batch right from the dough.
Just when it all looks hopeless, Paul writes one little word: "But." And God, who is rich in mercy, steps in.

cards.question: Paul says God, who is rich in mercy, acts because of His great ___ for us.

cards.text: God doesn't patch us up or hand us a pep talk. He made us alive with Christ.

cards.question: Paul says God waited until we had cleaned up our lives, and then He made us alive with Christ.

cards.text: Paul doesn't even finish his thought before he bursts out, "It is by grace you have been saved!" Then he keeps going: God raised us up with Christ.

cards.question: After God raised us up with Christ, where does Paul say God seated us?

answers.text: With Him in the heavenly realms
At His feet here on earth

cards.question: Paul says God did all this so that in the coming ages He could show off how hard His people worked.

cards.text: No, it's the surpassing riches of His grace, shown by His kindness to us in Christ Jesus. Then that grace line comes back, and this time Paul adds how it comes: through faith, and not from yourselves.

cards.question: Being saved is not from yourselves, Paul says. It is the ___ of God.

cards.text: And it's not by works, either. Good news for me, friend: I stamped crooked cookies for YEARS in a junk drawer, and if it came down to my work, I'd still be stuck behind the takeout menus.

cards.question: Paul says being saved is not by works. What does that mean no one can do?

cards.text: So do good works even matter? Paul says we are God's workmanship, created in Christ Jesus, and let me tell you, baker, God doesn't stamp crooked.

cards.question: We are God's workmanship, created in Christ Jesus. What does Paul say we were created to do?

answers.text: Good works God prepared in advance
Good works that earn His grace
Good works that pay off our sins
